setting: A student asks at the campus print shop why her print jobs are blocked and how to add quota.
narrator_intro: Listen to a conversation between a student and a staff member at the campus print shop.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Hi. I tried to print my poster for class, but the system says I've exceeded my print quota.

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Let me check your account. May I see your student ID?

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Sure. I still need twenty color pages today. Is there a way to add more quota?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Yes. Undergraduates get a free black-and-white allotment each term, but color is pay-as-you-go. You can buy a ten-dollar top-up here or online.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Can I pay with my campus card?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: Campus card or credit card both work. After you pay, wait about two minutes for the quota to refresh before you send the job again.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: My professor wants it on eleven-by-seventeen paper. Do you have that in color?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: We do, but large color sheets only print on the plotter by the window—not the regular color copiers. I'll unlock that queue after your top-up posts.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Perfect. One more thing—if the poster looks faded, can I reprint for free?

dialogue.speaker: speaker2
dialogue.text: If it's a machine error, yes—bring the bad copy back the same day and we'll reprint. If you just change the design, you'll use more quota.

dialogue.speaker: speaker1
dialogue.text: Got it. I'll buy the top-up now.

narrator_outro: Now get ready to answer the questions.

questions.narrator_text: What is the conversation mainly about?

options.text: Fixing a print-quota problem for a class poster
Borrowing a laptop from the library

questions.explanation: She cannot print because of quota; he explains top-ups and large-format color printing.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing A—nothing about laptop checkout is discussed.
questions.correctAnswer: Fixing a print-quota problem for a class poster

Use only the black-and-white machines forever
Buy a ten-dollar top-up at the shop or online
Wait until next term for an automatic reset only

questions.commonMistake: Choosing B—term allotment is for black-and-white; she needs color today.
questions.correctAnswer: Buy a ten-dollar top-up at the shop or online

questions.commonMistake: Choosing A because color copiers exist—they are not for that paper size.
questions.correctAnswer: On the plotter by the window
